title: Unit – 1 : Session – 2 : SLO – 1  |  Define, Declare and Access a Structure
sections: 1. struct — a structure is defined using the struct keyword.
2. member declarations (data members) — struct StructName { members };
4. dot (.) — members are accessed with the dot operator via a structure variable.
5. arrow (->) — members are accessed with the arrow operator via a pointer to a structure.
9. single (user-defined) — structures group different types into one user-defined type.
10. semicolon — structure definitions end with a semicolon.
1. Student record: struct Student { char name[50]; int roll; float marks; };  struct Student s = {"Asha", 12, 89.5};  printf("%s %d %.1f", s.name, s.roll, s.marks);
2. Three employees: struct Emp { char name[50]; float salary; };  struct Emp e[3];  for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) scanf("%s %f", e[i].name, &e[i].salary);  // access: e[i].name, e[i].salary
3. Book with pointer: struct Book { char title[50]; float price; };  struct Book b = {"C Programming", 450};  struct Book *ptr = &b;  printf("%s %.2f", ptr->title, ptr->price);
